name_zh: 八萬四千塔 (無憂王堵波)
proposed: unidentified; candidate Panch-Pahari mound C, S of Patna (Cunningham)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI p. 157: mound C at Panch-Pahari from Faxian's 3 li S of the city, curved bricks give c. 100-ft stūpa; nothing ties it to Aśoka; Beglar's Bhika Pahari for the same mounds withdrawn (ASR VIII Note)
Cunningham ASR XI p. 159 infers spot G at Panch-Pahari from the pilgrims' descriptions, nothing found; Kumrahar has actual fragments

mizutani: no modern identification (SE of old Pāṭaliputra)
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 27: unnamed small brick mound SE of Patna, no evidence; Cunningham ASR XI p. 162: not found; Beal, Dey give no site; gazetteers silent
no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

proposed: Tillara (Bulandi mound W of the village)
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 33: Sangin Masjid jamb inscription naming Teladaka (read by Cunningham); Cunningham ASR VIII pref., XI pp. 162-166 (distances reconciled, Bulandi mound measured); Patna 1907: Pāla inscription naming Tailadhaka

Beglar ASR VIII p. 36 (route followed without correction), adopted by Cunningham ASR XI p. 162, XV p. iv, XVI pp. 39-40, abandoning his 1871 site NW of Wazirganj; Pravara-giri-guhā named in the Barābar cave inscription (ASR I)

Beglar ASR VIII pp. 36-39; Cunningham ASR XV p. iv, XVI pp. v, 45-46: monastery with back wall against the hill, summit stūpa of stūpa-stamped bricks with Gupta seals "Tathāgatasya Buddhasya", Kunwa < Guṇamati; Majumdar, Dey; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

Beglar ASR VIII pp. 39-40 (20 li SW on the ground; temple, colossal Buddha, creed inscription; 12 mi on to Gayā fits); Cunningham ASR XVI pp. 46-49 concurs, drops his Bithawa; stūpa-shaped peak, granite pillars; Dey; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

mizutani: Mora hill, c. 3 mi NE of Bodh Gayā
proposed: Mora range; cave on NW slope of Dhongra Hill
basis: Cunningham Mora Pahar; Gaya 1906/1957 (Oldham): cave with Buddhist image, terrace, seven stūpa remains on summit, distance 14-15 li

proposed: Bodh Gayā precinct; stone railing = Aśoka's wall (rearranged)
basis: all authorities; Cunningham ASR I, III (tree terrace, Vajrāsana); Gaya 1906: pillar height 9 ft 10 in vs 10-ft wall, Aśokan-character inscriptions, votive stūpas
Cunningham ASR I, III, XI p. 145 (theodolite height 160 ft vs 160-170; base vs 20 paces; E rooms later as Xuanzang says), XVI (promenade); Watters objects; Gaya 1906 restoration finds echo

proposed: open: Teskar Tal (Cunningham), Urel tank (Xuanzang's E bearing), or Muchharin
basis: Cunningham ASR I p. 10 Buchhokar Tal, then ASR XI p. 147 Teskar Tal reading W for E (pl. XL: C = Muchilinda's tank, D Urel Tal = Uruvilvā tank); Gaya 1906/1957: cult at Muchharin
no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site
Cunningham ASR I p. 13 describes only the Bakror pillar; depends on 09.01.03
Cunningham, Beal, Vivien, Dey unanimous; gazetteers incidental

name_zh: 屈屈吒播陀山 (窶盧播陀山)
basis: Cunningham himself moves from three hills 1/2 mi N (ASR I) to Murali 3 mi NNE (ASR XV, summit basement), still argued from the name; Gaya 1906/1957: Stein's Hasra (bearings, summit stūpa) conclusive vs Kurkihar; Banerji's Gurpa (Gurupāda, cleft, three peaks) favoured by Majumdar, Dey
Cunningham ASR III pp. 139-140 Budhain: no stūpa or cave found; rejected by Majumdar (Stein, Jeshtiban position)
Cunningham 1871, ASR III; Beal, Watters; Gaya 1906/1957 (Stein): two main springs with stūpa mound, 2 mi SW of Jethian

name_zh: 小孤山 (石室・阿素洛宮)
proposed: Asura palace = Rajpind cave, Chandu hill
basis: Gaya 1906/1957 (Stein): large cave with deep fissure, ancient walled road from Khiri; Beglar ASR VIII pp. 84, 89 had not found it

name_zh: 矩奢掲羅補羅城 (上茅宮城)
mizutani: Old Rājagṛha (Girivraja) in the hill-girt valley
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 22-24: ramparts surveyed (inner 24,500 ft; outer wall 13 ft thick; 150 li read 50); ASR III p. 143 walls 18 ft thick at S gate; HU11 repeats

proposed: Sailagiri spur with the Bimbisāra road (Chhathagiri)
basis: Beglar ASR VIII Note pp. xiv-xxi retracts his Son Bhandar caves and finds caves, topes on the Sailagiri spur (but takes the ramp for a defence wall); Patna 1907 (Sen): causeway with two stūpa traces; Cunningham Sailagiri

mizutani: cave on N face of Vaibhāra (Takakusu)
proposed: cave behind Jarasandh-ki-baithak, N/NE face of Vaibhāra
basis: Cunningham ASR III pp. 140-142 found and cleared it (Jan 1872), abandoning Ratnagiri; Beglar ASR VIII p. 89 accepts; Xuanzang's "Vipula" unresolved

mizutani: = Faxian's 調達石窟, 3 li E of old N gate
proposed: cave M on the slope of Vipula
basis: Beglar ASR VIII p. 90: cave M on Cunningham's plan (ASR III pl. 41), in Mizutani's position; no description

name_zh: 阿闍多設咄路王舍利塔
mizutani: mound E of the road, now Muslim cemetery (Takakusu)
basis: no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

proposed: N side of Baibhāra (Beglar's cavern, Stein's caves or Marshall's spur), not Son Bhandar
basis: Beglar ASR VIII pp. 92-99 (W-facing cavern on N slope, stairs, caitya W); Patna 1907 Stein, Marshall; against Cunningham ASR III p. 143 "absolute certainty" for Son Bhandar (chisel-cut, socket holes)
no authority, gazetteer or survey report gives a site

name_zh: 無憂王堵波・石柱 (迦蘭陀池西北)
proposed: SW of New Rājagṛha (Takakusu's area; Cunningham's hollow mound)
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 24-25: robbed circular mound outside SW corner of New Rajgir, no pillar; same area as Takakusu
Cunningham ASR I pp. 28-35: two inscriptions naming Nālandā on the site, monastery field measured, sub-sites lettered; all authorities; gazetteers echo

name_zh: 精舍 (如來三月說法處, 那爛陀伽藍西)
mizutani: probably the Mūlagandhakuṭī among caityas W of the monasteries
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 29-30: mound A 63 ft high, W of monastery, temple walls excavated; Spooner's Site 3 excavation (Patna 1907) identifies the same mound
Cunningham ASR I pp. 28-29: mound with large Buddha sculpture, from bearing and distance only; gazetteers silent
Watters, Beal agree on Nāla; Cunningham (1871, ASR I), Dey only c. 4 mi SE of Nālandā

Cunningham ASR I (goose figure and seals by the single stūpa), III pp. 144-150 (Haṃsa monastery terrace, route), XI; Beglar ASR VIII p. 78 cave; Patna 1907 echoes; Faxian equation conceded by Cunningham ASR XV p. 7

Beglar ASR VIII pp. 108-113; Cunningham ASR XV pp. 4-10 final view (NE bearing, Pigeon's House name, terraced hill S of village, stūpa bricks E of monastery mound, Gupta monastic seal "saṅghasa") after ASR XI's Bihār/Soh-sarai; both need the emendation

proposed: Parbati hill, site A (dargah of Haji Chandar)
basis: Cunningham ASR XV pp. 8-9 (temple at centre of hill, now the dargah; Beglar's cells) after ASR XI p. 189 Bihār hill; follows 09.03.13; Gaya 1906/1957 echo

name_zh: 一伽藍 (孤山東南四十餘里)
proposed: unidentified (Aphsar if Kapotaka = Parbati; Tetrawa if Bihār)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 184-189 Tetrawa (inscriptions naming Tentaḍi-grāma) from Bihār; ASR XV pp. 10-11 Aphsar reading 4 li, nothing at 40 li; Gaya 1906 "doubt" repeats Cunningham's caveat
Cunningham ASR XV pp. 12-13 (bearing, distance, wooded route), revising 1871 Daryapur; Beal; Monghyr 1909/1960 echo; no remains
Cunningham ASR XV pp. 12-15 (Balguzar Jhil = lake N of stūpa, statues in N mounds, onward distance to Monghyr), revising 1871 Rohinila; Dey, Beal report; Monghyr 1909/1960 echo
